title: Understanding Computing Basics
objective: Explain the input–processing–storage–output cycle every computer uses to get work done.
lessonSummary:
Every computer, no matter how complex, is really doing the same basic cycle: Input (getting information in — typing, clicking, a camera, a scanner), Processing (the computer's processor acting on that information, following instructions), Storage (keeping information for later, either temporarily in memory or permanently on a drive), and Output (giving a result back — on screen, printed, played as sound, or sent somewhere else).

Thinking in this cycle is a useful workplace habit: when something goes wrong, ask yourself which stage failed. Did the input never register? Did processing hang? Was nothing saved? Did the output never actually reach where it needed to go? That question alone solves a surprising number of everyday tech problems.
